column1: # Short titles for recipe steps (schema.org HowToStep.name), English side.
# Written by hand and matched one-to-one with the Turkish titles in
# veri/adim_adlari.tsv. Format: title <TAB> the step's full text.
# If the text changes the match is lost and the step simply has no title —
# a wrong summary never goes live.

column2: Wash the ginger and slice it thinly, skin on.

column1: Bring to the boil with water
column2: Put the slices and water in a small pot and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat down and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Strain into a cup; once it has cooled a little, add lemon and honey if you like.
Warm the milk in a small pot; do not let it boil.
Add the turmeric, pepper and cinnamon if using, and whisk well.
Heat for 2–3 minutes over low heat, stirring.
Pour into a cup and add the honey once it has cooled slightly.
Boil the water and take it off the heat.
Put the linden in a teapot or cup and pour the water over it.
Cover and steep for 5–10 minutes.
Strain and drink, with honey or lemon if you like.
Put the chamomile in a cup or teapot.
Pour the water over it and cover with a saucer.
Steep for 5–10 minutes.
Strain and drink warm.

column1: Wash the mint, put in glass
column2: Wash the mint leaves and put them in a cup.
Pour the water over them and cover the cup.
Wait 5 minutes.
Remove the leaves or strain, and drink.
Put the thyme in a cup or teapot.
Pour the water over it and cover.
Strain and add honey once it has cooled a little.
Break the stems to fit your teapot.
Pour the water over them.
Strain and drink, with lemon and honey if you like.
Lightly crush the seeds in a mortar or with the flat of a knife.
Put them in a cup and pour the water over them.
Cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain and drink.
Lightly crush the aniseed.
Put it in a cup and pour the water over it.
Boil the water and let it cool for 2–3 minutes.
Put the rose hips in a teapot and pour the water over them.
Steep for 10 minutes.
Strain through muslin or a very fine sieve so that none of the hairs around the seeds remain.
Put the leaves in a cup or teapot.
Pour the water over them and cover.
Break the cinnamon stick in two and put it in a small pot with the water.
Bring to the boil, then simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Take off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Add the washed basil, stems and all; cover and steep for 15 minutes.
Strain; while it is still hot, stir in the sugar until it dissolves.
When cool, add the lemon juice; it will turn from purple to pink. Chill and serve.
Lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife.
Mix the coffee, water, cardamom and sugar if using in a cezve.
Cook over low heat without stirring until it foams up.
Spoon the foam into the cup, bring the rest up once more and pour.
Wash the nettles wearing gloves and remove the tough stems.
Fry the onion in the olive oil until soft; add the rice or flour and stir for a minute.
Add the water and nettles; once boiling, simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend if you like; season with salt and chilli flakes.
Put the rosemary in a cup.
Put the flowers in a teapot or a mug with a strainer.
Pour boiling water over them and cover, so the essential oils do not escape with the steam.
Steep for 5–10 minutes and strain. Drink half an hour before bed.

column1: Put the root in the pot
column2: Put the root in a teapot and pour boiling water over it.
Steep covered for 10–15 minutes.
Strain; drink 30–60 minutes before bed.
Put the leaves and flowers in a cup or teapot.

column1: Put the root in a jar
column2: Put the root in a jar or glass and pour the water over it.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 2–3 hours, stirring now and then.
Strain through a fine sieve.
Sip it without heating.

column1: Roast the root in a pan
column2: Roast the root in a dry pan over low heat, stirring, for 5–8 minutes until dark brown.
Let it cool, then grind it coarsely in a mortar or coffee grinder.
Put it in a small pot with the water, bring to the boil and simmer gently for 5 minutes.

column1: Strain, add milk if you like
column2: Strain through a fine sieve and add milk if you like.
Add the sumac to the cold water, cover and leave in the fridge for 4–6 hours or overnight.
Strain through muslin, squeezing the sumac gently.
Stir in the sugar or honey until dissolved.
Serve cold.
Wash the fruit and put it in a pot with the water.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the skins split.
Strain, pressing the fruit gently; discard the stones.
Add the sugar (and cloves) while hot, boil for 5 more minutes, cool and keep in the fridge.
Put the hibiscus in a jug and add the cold water.
Cover and leave in the fridge for 6–8 hours or overnight.
Strain and add honey and mint if you like.
Drink cold.
Put the tahini in a small bowl.
Add the molasses.
Stir with a fork until thick and glossy.
Serve with bread.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Crush lightly in a mortar and put in a cup.
Pour the water over, cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Warm the seeds in a dry pan for a minute until fragrant.
Crush them roughly in a mortar.
Mix with the honey.
Eat straight away or keep in a small jar.
Put the leaves in a cup.
Pour the water over and cover.
Break the leaves in half and put them in a small pot with the water.
Bring to the boil and simmer gently for 3–5 minutes.
Take off the heat and rest for 5 minutes.
Remove the leaves and drink.
Pound the mastic with a pinch of sugar in a mortar until powdered.
Whisk the rice flour and cornflour with a cup of cold milk until smooth.
Heat the rest of the milk with the sugar, add the starch mixture and cook, stirring constantly, for 10–12 minutes until thick.
Stir in the mastic for one more minute, pour into bowls and chill.
Put the leaves in a small pot with the water.
Bring to the boil and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes.
Strain.
Drink once warm; add a little honey if it is too bitter.
Seed the pomegranates and press or blend the arils, then strain through muslin; you should get 2–2.5 litres of juice.
Bring the juice to the boil in a wide pot and skim the foam.
Simmer over low heat, stirring now and then, for 2–3 hours until reduced to a quarter and syrupy.
When it coats the back of a spoon (add the salt if using), take it off the heat and pour into glass bottles while hot.
Pick over the buds, wash them and let them wilt in the shade for half a day.
Layer them with the salt in a jar and leave for 7–10 days, shaking daily and pouring off the bitter liquid.
Rinse well to remove the salt.
Mix the vinegar and water, pack the capers into a clean jar and cover completely; they are ready in 2–3 weeks in a cool place.
Crush the garlic with the salt in a mortar.
Leave the crushed garlic to stand for 10 minutes.
Stir it into the yogurt.
Finish with dried mint and a few drops of olive oil if you like.
Grind the flaxseed in a coffee grinder (whole seeds pass through undigested).
Cook the oats in the milk or water for 4–5 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the flaxseed.
Top with fruit or cinnamon and drink a glass of water with it.
Boil the water in the lower kettle and put the tea in the upper pot.
Pour about a cup of the boiling water into the upper pot.
Turn the heat to its lowest and brew the upper pot on top of the kettle for 10–15 minutes.
Pour the brew first and top up with hot water, light or strong as you like.
If using root, put it in a small pot with the water, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
If using flowering tops, pour just-boiled water over them, cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Drink once warm.
Keep the artichoke hearts in lemon water so they do not darken.
Soften the onion in the olive oil, add the carrot and peas and stir for 3–4 minutes.
Arrange the artichokes in the pot, fill them with the vegetables and add the sugar, salt, lemon juice and hot water.
Cover and cook over low heat for 30–35 minutes until tender; serve cold with dill.
Mix the cocoa and sugar with a few spoons of milk into a paste.
Add the rest of the milk and heat gently, stirring; do not boil.
Add the cinnamon.
Whisk until frothy and drink hot.
Warm the milk in a small pot.
Whisk in the maca and cinnamon.
Heat gently for 2–3 minutes, stirring.
Add honey once it has cooled a little.
Wash the berries; thaw them if frozen.
Blend with one cup of the water.
Strain through a fine sieve to remove seeds and skins.
Stir in the remaining water and the honey; drink cold or at room temperature.
Put the flowers in a cup.

column1: Strain, add honey if you like
column2: Strain through muslin or a coffee filter and add honey if you like.
Steep for no more than 5 minutes; longer makes it bitter.

column1: Put the sprigs in the glass
column2: Put the twigs in a cup.
Add the root to the cold water, cover and leave in the fridge for 6–8 hours.
Strain through muslin.
Pour from jug to jug from a height to make it froth.
Drink cold; no sugar needed, the root is already sweet.
Shake the flowers gently to remove insects; do not wash them or the scent goes. Cut off the thick stalks.
Boil the water with the sugar to make a syrup and let it cool.
Add the flowers and lemon slices, cover and leave somewhere cool for 24–48 hours.
Strain through muslin and bottle; dilute 1 part cordial with 5–6 parts cold water.

column1: Put the herb in the glass
column2: Put the herb in a cup.
Strain and drink before a meal.
Crush the seeds lightly in a mortar.
Put them in a small pot with the water, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Soak the saffron in half a small glass of warm water for at least an hour.
Cook the rice in the water for 25–30 minutes until it falls apart; add the sugar.
Mix the cornflour with a little cold water and add it with the saffron water; stir for 5 minutes until thick.
Pour into bowls and garnish with pine nuts, currants and pomegranate once cool.
Put the cloves, cinnamon and orange peel in a small pot with the water.
Bring to the boil and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Put the muña in a cup.
Steep for 5 minutes.
Strain and drink after a meal.
Remove and discard all the leaves; only the stalks are used.
Peel off the fibrous outer skin and cut the stalks into finger lengths.

column1: Pack in a jar with garlic
column2: Pack them tightly into a jar with the garlic.
Mix the water, vinegar and salt and pour over to cover completely; leave in a cool place for 7–10 days.
Take the berries out of their papery husks and wash them; discard any green, unripe ones.
Mix the berries with the sugar and leave for 2 hours.
Add the water, bring to the boil and simmer for 20–25 minutes until thick.
Add the lemon juice and pour into jars while hot.
If they are in the shell, crack the shells and pick out the seeds.
Spread the seeds in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast at 160 °C for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Sprinkle with salt while hot; store in a closed jar once cool.
Put the petals in a cup.
Wash the jujubes and score them with a knife or cut them in half.

column1: Bring to the boil with water
column2: Put them in a pot with the water and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes.
Strain and drink hot; you can eat the softened fruit, removing the stones.
Crumble the leaves and put them in a small pot with the water.
Take off the heat as soon as it boils.
Pound the mahleb kernels to a powder just before using.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and mahleb; add the milk, butter and one egg and knead into a soft dough.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into three, braid and rest on a tray for 20 more minutes.
Brush with egg yolk, sprinkle with seeds and bake at 180 °C for 25–30 minutes.
Crush the berries lightly in a mortar.
Put them in a small pot with the water and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Strain and drink once warm.
Wash the figs and put them in a bowl.
Leave overnight at room temperature.
In the morning, eat the figs on an empty stomach and drink the water.
Pick the berries off the stalks and wash them; freeze overnight to reduce bitterness.
Cook the berries and apple with the water for 15 minutes until soft.
Press through a sieve, leaving seeds and skins behind.
Boil the purée with the sugar for 20–25 minutes until thick, add the lemon juice and pour into jars while hot.
Separate the seeds from the pumpkin fibres and wash them.
Dry them well with a clean cloth.
Toss with the oil and salt and spread on a tray in one layer.
Roast at 160 °C for 15–20 minutes, stirring now and then, until lightly golden.

column1: Put the silk in the glass
column2: Cut the silk and put it in a cup.
Strain and drink; keep drinking plenty of water during the day.
Strain and drink in the evening before bed.
Strain and drink; drink plenty of water during the day.
Put the mate in a teapot or cup and moisten it first with a few spoons of cold water.
Pour over the hot (not boiling) water.
Lightly grate the zest with the coarse side of a grater, then peel the oranges in strips.
Roll the strips, thread them on string and soak for 2 days, changing the water 2–3 times a day to remove bitterness.
Blanch the rolls in boiling water for 10 minutes and drain.
Make a syrup with the sugar and water, add the rolls and boil for 30–40 minutes until thick; add the lemon juice and pour into jars while hot.
Soften the goji in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Put the yogurt in a bowl.
Scatter the goji and broken walnuts on top.
Drizzle with honey and serve.
Soak the almonds overnight in plenty of water; drain and rinse in the morning.
Blend the almonds with the 4 cups of water for 1–2 minutes.
Strain through muslin or a nut-milk bag, squeezing well.
Blend again with dates to sweeten if you like; drink within 3 days, kept in the fridge.
Rinse the barley several times.
Put it in a pot with the water and lemon peel, bring to the boil and simmer for 30 minutes.
Strain; use the barley in soup or salad.
Add honey or sugar while hot and the lemon juice once cool; drink cold.
Rinse brined leaves several times to remove the salt; blanch fresh leaves in boiling water for 1–2 minutes.
Soften the onion in the olive oil, add the pine nuts, then the washed rice, currants and spices and stir for 5 minutes.
Put a dessertspoon of filling on the veined side of each leaf, roll tightly and pack into a pot.
Add the lemon juice and hot water, weigh down with an upturned plate and cook over low heat for 40–45 minutes; serve cold.

column1: Put oat straw in the glass
column2: Put the oat straw in a cup.
Crush the seeds in a mortar.
Put them in a cup, pour the water over and cover.
Strain and drink between meals.
Pick over the chicory, wash it well and drain.
Chop the leaves roughly and slice the onion into thin rings.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the chicory and onion with the dressing and serve at once.
Wash the leaves and dry them well.
Remove the stalks and chop the leaves very finely.
Mix with the coconut, shallot, salt and chilli.
Add the lime juice just before serving.

column1: Put the cones in the glass
column2: Put the cones in a cup.
Steep for 10–15 minutes.
Strain and drink half an hour before bed.
